overall.label: Overall
overall.description: A weighted blend of every category. Adjust the weights to match what matters to you.

categories.label: Safety
categories.question: Where is reported crime lowest?
categories.caveat: Police-recorded offences per 100,000 residents, averaged over 2023–2025. Areas many people visit (centre, nightlife, stations) read higher than what residents experience; the police note a high rate can also reflect liveliness. Unreported crime isn't included.

metrics.label: Neighbourhood offences
metrics.description: ‘Kieztaten’: the police's neighbourhood-related offences — e.g. assault, threats, robbery, burglary, vandalism of cars.

metrics.label: Assaults
metrics.description: Bodily harm, all kinds.

metrics.label: Robbery
metrics.description: Robbery, incl. street and handbag robbery.

metrics.label: Home burglary
metrics.description: Break-ins into homes.

metrics.label: All reported offences
metrics.description: Every offence recorded in the area, incl. those against visitors and businesses.

metrics.label: Bike theft
metrics.description: Bicycles stolen.

metrics.label: Car theft & break-ins
metrics.description: Cars stolen plus thefts from or of parts of cars.

categories.label: Road safety
categories.question: Where do the fewest road accidents happen?
categories.caveat: Accidents with personal injury recorded by the police in 2025, per 10 km of public street. Main roads carry through traffic, so their accidents count where they happen, not where the people involved live.

metrics.label: Injury accidents
metrics.description: Road accidents in which someone was hurt.
metrics.berlin_method: All of Berlin: 13,275 in 2025 over 6,197 km of street

metrics.label: Killed or seriously injured
metrics.description: Accidents in which someone died or was seriously injured.
metrics.berlin_method: All of Berlin: 1,658 in 2025 over 6,197 km of street

metrics.label: Involving pedestrians or cyclists
metrics.description: Injury accidents in which a pedestrian or cyclist was involved.
metrics.berlin_method: All of Berlin: 6,216 in 2025 over 6,197 km of street

categories.label: Affluence
categories.question: Which areas have the highest social and economic status?
categories.caveat: A proxy, not a measure of wealth: median wealth and income aren't published for neighbourhoods in Germany. We combine the Senate's social-status index (built from indicators such as unemployment and welfare receipt) with official land values at residents' homes. Both describe places, not any person, and areas change.

metrics.label: Social-status index
metrics.description: Monitoring Soziale Stadtentwicklung 2023: the Senate's status class of each planning area, weighted by its residents.
metrics.berlin_method: Berlin, weighted by residents of indexed planning areas

metrics.label: Land-value index
metrics.unit: 0–100, vs. land of the same density
metrics.description: Where the standard land values (Bodenrichtwerte 2026) at the area's homes rank among Berlin's residential zones of the same kind — houses compared with houses, blocks of flats with flats. 100 = Berlin's priciest land of its kind.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Typical land value
metrics.unit: EUR/m² of plot, median at homes
metrics.description: Median Bodenrichtwert at the area's homes (context, not scored: it mostly reflects how densely land may be built on).
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Income per taxpayer
metrics.description: Total income per taxpayer from the income-tax statistics.
metrics.city_note: Berlin as a whole: €91.1 billion total income of 2,017,622 taxpayers with positive income; the median taxpayer is in the €30,000–35,000 bracket. The report has no district breakdown.

categories.label: Education
categories.question: Where are school results strongest and schools closest?
categories.caveat: Literacy isn't published below national level. School results (Abitur share, leavers without a qualification, Gymnasium recommendations) are per district and counted where the school is, so all areas of a district share them; nearby schools and Kitas are measured from homes (OpenStreetMap).

metrics.label: School leavers with Abitur
metrics.description: Share of leavers from general schools in the district with the Abitur, 2024/25.

metrics.label: Leavers without a qualification
metrics.description: Share leaving general schools without the Berufsbildungsreife, 2024/25.

metrics.label: Gymnasium recommendations
metrics.description: Primary pupils with a Gymnasium/ISS recommendation (Förderprognose), 2024/25.

metrics.label: Schools within 1 km
metrics.description: Schools within 1 km of the typical home.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Kitas within 500 m
metrics.description: Kitas (day-care centres) within 500 m of the typical home.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

categories.label: Healthcare
categories.question: Where are hospitals, doctors and pharmacies closest?
categories.caveat: Mapped in OpenStreetMap: hospitals include specialist clinics; doctors include dentists and clinics. Straight-line distances from homes.

metrics.label: Nearest hospital
metrics.description: Distance from the typical home to the nearest hospital.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Doctors within 1 km
metrics.description: Doctors, dentists and clinics within 1 km of the typical home.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Pharmacies within 500 m
metrics.description: Pharmacies within 500 m of the typical home.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

categories.label: Amenities
categories.question: Where are cafés, shops, culture and sport within walking distance?
categories.caveat: Counted from OpenStreetMap within walking distance of homes. Nightlife is shown but not scored — whether it's a plus depends on you.

metrics.label: Cafés & restaurants within 500 m
metrics.description: Cafés, restaurants and bakeries within 500 m of the typical home.

metrics.label: Everyday shops within 500 m
metrics.description: Supermarkets, pharmacies and doctors within 500 m of the typical home.

metrics.label: Culture within 1.5 km
metrics.description: Museums, theatres, cinemas, arts centres and libraries within 1.5 km.

metrics.label: Sport within 1 km
metrics.description: Gyms, pools and sports centres within 1 km.

metrics.label: Bars & clubs within 1 km
metrics.description: Bars, pubs, clubs and beer gardens within 1 km (context only, not scored).

categories.label: Parks & nature
categories.question: Where are parks, water and forest closest?
categories.caveat: Green-space supply from the Senate's environmental-justice atlas (data from 2020); park, water and forest distances and playgrounds from OpenStreetMap.

metrics.label: Green-space supply
metrics.description: Public green space per resident, Berlin-relative class, weighted by residents.

metrics.label: Nearest park (≥ 1 ha)
metrics.description: Distance from the typical home to the edge of a public park of at least 1 ha.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Nearest water or forest
metrics.description: Distance to the nearest lake, river or canal (≥ 1 ha) or forest (≥ 5 ha).

metrics.label: Playgrounds within 500 m
metrics.description: Playgrounds within 500 m of the typical home.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

categories.label: Public transport
categories.question: Where are S-/U-Bahn, tram and bus closest and the centre quickest to reach?
categories.caveat: Rail and tram stops with weekday-peak service (VBB timetable); all stops from OpenStreetMap; travel time to Alexanderplatz routed over the VBB timetable.

metrics.label: Nearest S-/U-Bahn or tram
metrics.description: Distance to the nearest rail, S-/U-Bahn or tram stop with weekday-peak service.

metrics.label: Stops within 500 m
metrics.description: Public transport stops within 500 m of the typical home (OSM; a stop's platforms may count separately).
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: To Alexanderplatz
metrics.description: Public-transport time from the area's residential centre to Alexanderplatz.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

categories.label: Quiet & clean air
categories.question: Where is traffic noise, air pollution and summer heat lowest?
categories.caveat: Berlin-relative classes from the environmental-justice atlas 2023/24 (noise 2022, air 2023, heat 2022), weighted by where residents live. Not absolute health limits.

metrics.label: Traffic noise
metrics.description: Berlin-relative traffic-noise burden (2022), weighted by residents.

metrics.label: Air pollution
metrics.description: Berlin-relative NO₂/particulate burden (2023), weighted by residents.

metrics.label: Summer heat
metrics.description: Berlin-relative day and night heat stress (2022), weighted by residents.

categories.label: Parking
categories.question: Where is it easiest to park a car?
categories.caveat: Paid-parking streets are detected from parking ticket machines mapped in OpenStreetMap; car-park areas are as complete as OSM mapping. Density stands in for parking pressure. On-street spaces aren't counted anywhere officially.

metrics.label: Homes in paid-parking streets
metrics.description: Share of homes with a parking ticket machine within 150 m (a paid-parking zone).
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Car parks within 300 m
metrics.description: Area of mapped car parks (incl. marked street-side parking) within 300 m of homes.
metrics.berlin_method: Mean of all areas, weighted by residents

metrics.label: Population density
metrics.description: Registered residents per km² — more residents, more cars competing for space.

categories.label: Affordability
categories.question: Where are asking rents lowest?
categories.caveat: Median asking rent of the district (IBB 2025), so all areas of a district share it. 80% of offers fall within the district's range shown with each area.

metrics.label: Median asking rent
metrics.description: Median asking rent of the district, 2025 (IBB).

sources.title: Statistischer Bericht L IV 3 – j / 22: Lohn- und Einkommensteuerstatistik im Land Berlin 2022, Tabelle 1
sources.used_for: Berlin-wide taxpayers and total income (Gesamtbetrag der Einkünfte), shown as the city reference for income.
sources.caveat: Berlin as a whole only; the report has no district breakdown.

sources.title: Blickpunkt Schule, Bericht 2025/2026 — Tab. 3.2.3 (Förderprognose) and Abb. 5.1.2 (Schulabschlüsse in den Bezirken)
sources.publisher: Senatsverwaltung für Bildung, Jugend und Familie, Referat I C
sources.used_for: Per district: school leavers from general schools by qualification, and primary pupils by secondary-school recommendation.
sources.caveat: District figures, counted where the school is (pupils may live in another district). The report notes that school populations differ a lot between districts.

sources.title: Bodenrichtwerte zum 01.01.2026 (Vektordaten, WGS84)
sources.used_for: Standard land value (EUR/m² of plot) of the residential, core and mixed zones that the area's home sample points lie in.
sources.caveat: Bodenrichtwerte are typical land prices for a zone, not values of individual properties. Land for houses and for blocks of flats are different markets, so each home is only compared with land of the same kind.

sources.title: IBB Wohnungsmarktbericht 2025 — Tabellenband, Tab. 25 ‘Angebotsmieten nach Bezirken 2025’
sources.publisher: Investitionsbank Berlin (IBB); data: VALUE Marktdatenbank, RegioKontext GmbH
sources.used_for: Median asking rent (net cold) per district, and the range that 80% of offers fall into.
sources.caveat: District medians from listings, not signed contracts. Neighbourhoods within a district differ; the range shows how much.

sources.title: Monitoring Soziale Stadtentwicklung 2023 — Tabelle 1: Gesamtindex Soziale Ungleichheit (Status/Dynamik-Index) auf Planungsraum-Ebene
sources.publisher: Senatsverwaltung für Stadtentwicklung, Bauen und Wohnen Berlin
sources.used_for: Status-Index class (1 high – 4 very low) and residents of each of the 542 planning areas, weighted by residents up to Bezirksregionen.
sources.caveat: The status index combines four indicators of residents' social and economic situation (e.g. unemployment, welfare receipt). It describes averages, not people. The Senate doesn't index 6 planning areas (under 300 residents or statistical outliers); they're left out of the average.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap — Geofabrik ‘berlin-latest-free’ GeoPackage
sources.publisher: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0), extract by Geofabrik GmbH
sources.used_for: Cafés, shops, doctors, bars, culture and sport venues; residential land; lakes, rivers and forests.
sources.caveat: Community-mapped: very complete in Berlin but not official. Distances are straight lines from homes, so real walks are a little longer.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap — Berlin extract (Geofabrik, free GeoPackage), 2026-11-12
sources.publisher: © OpenStreetMap contributors; extract by Geofabrik GmbH
sources.used_for: Hospitals, doctors, pharmacies, schools, Kitas, playgrounds, parks, stops, parking ticket machines, car parks and streets, measured from 100 m sample points on residential land.
sources.caveat: As complete as volunteer mapping; straight-line distances understate real walks a little.

sources.title: Kriminalitätsatlas Berlin — Fallzahlen und Häufigkeitszahlen 2016–2025
sources.used_for: Offence rates per 100,000 residents (neighbourhood offences, assault, robbery, burglary, bike and car crime, all offences), mean of 2023–2025, per Bezirksregion.
sources.caveat: Reported offences per 100,000 registered residents. Areas many people visit (centre, nightlife, transport hubs) read higher than what residents experience; the police note a high rate can also reflect liveliness and popularity.

sources.title: Lebensweltlich orientierte Räume (LOR) 2021 — Planungsräume (WGS84)
sources.publisher: Senatsverwaltung für Stadtentwicklung, Bauen und Wohnen / Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg
sources.used_for: Planning-area boundaries (area, centre points) and the official ‘Innere Stadt’ / ‘Äußere Stadt’ classification.
sources.caveat: Region centre points are population-weighted, i.e. where people live, not the geometric middle of parks or rail yards.

sources.title: Umweltgerechtigkeitsatlas 2023/2024 (Broschüre), ‘Aufschlüsselung der Planungsräume nach Belastungssituation’
sources.publisher: Senatsverwaltung für Mobilität, Verkehr, Klimaschutz und Umwelt
sources.used_for: Noise, air, heat and green-space burden class (low / medium / high) per Planungsraum, weighted by residents to Bezirksregionen.
sources.caveat: Classes are relative to the rest of Berlin (lowest quarter = low, highest quarter = high), not absolute health thresholds. The atlas's social-disadvantage indicator is deliberately not used.

sources.title: Unfallatlas — Unfallorte 2025 (Open Data)
sources.publisher: Statistische Ämter des Bundes und der Länder
sources.used_for: Location and severity of every police-recorded road accident with personal injury in Berlin, counted per Bezirksregion.
sources.caveat: Only accidents with personal injury. Accidents count where they happened; main roads carry through traffic.

sources.title: VBB GTFS timetable — weekday peak network (07:00–09:00)
sources.used_for: S-Bahn, U-Bahn, regional-rail and tram stops with peak-hour service.
sources.caveat: Buses are not counted: almost everyone in Berlin lives near one.
